criteria.criterion: docs/design/native-pr-landing.md gains text for N1: the exact comparison (merged tree against the verified fingerprint), the named state of a merged-but-refused job, and how the user moves it out of that state.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. §5.4 'Merged-content check (design; review 3 N1)' defines the comparison: the governed-content fingerprint of the merged commit's tree, computed under the rules at the job's base, against the verified fingerprint, with no diff branch. 'The refused state (N1)' names `merged-unverified` and says the user leaves it by re-verifying the job on the new tip as a new job. §5.7 point 3 links back to this.

criteria.criterion: The design states for N2 that the PR number, host, repository and pushed head live in the state directory in both modes. The status line no longer says 'Not yet re-reviewed' and cites review 3.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. §5.1 step 3 says the number, host, repository and pushed head are stored 'in the state directory, in both modes' in pr-link.json, and that the records schema does not change. The status line now cites design/reviews/native-pr-landing-review-3.md, and 'Not yet re-reviewed' is gone.

criteria.criterion: The design states for N3 what the stealth PR body keeps and drops, that the leak check covers the body, and that stealth pushes a neutral branch name. It also states how the push restriction to the job's own branch is checked.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. §5.1 step 3 lists what the stealth body keeps and what it drops. The §5.4 leak check now covers pull request body lines. A new 'Neutral branch name' bullet covers the branch name. A new §5.2 bullet, 'How "the job's own branch" is checked', says the guard compares for equality against the one allowed name stored for the job.

criteria.criterion: The design states for N4 which per-job checks run over the local store when several jobs are squashed in stealth mode.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. §5.6 'Earlier jobs in stealth (review 3 N4)' lists five checks: records valid and append-only (M4, M5); verdict a pass, with the job's own fingerprint; prediction before outcome (M23); the previous_job chain; and the secret scan. If any earlier job fails, none of the jobs is recorded as landed.

criteria.criterion: A new owned-mode module exists in athena-core. It stores and loads a PR link record (PR number, host, repository, head commit id, job id) under the job's state directory, outside the repository's records/.
criteria.evidence: I read the code. crates/athena-core/src/pr.rs defines PrLink with pr_number, host, repository, head and job, plus state and merged_commit. store_link and load_link use StateDir::job_dir(job)/pr-link.json, and job_dir is root/jobs/<id> in state.rs, so the file is outside records/. A round-trip test exists and passes.

criteria.criterion: The module has a push guard that refuses any branch other than the job's work branch and any non-fast-forward push. It has no force option.
criteria.evidence: I read the code. check_push returns WrongBranch when the branch is not the allowed branch or is empty. It returns NotFastForward when the remote head is not an ancestor of the local head; a git error counts as not an ancestor, so it is also refused. PushRequest has no force field.

criteria.criterion: The module has a merged-content check that returns a 'merged but not verified' result on a tree mismatch. The merge is found by the stored PR number and never by parsing trailers.
criteria.evidence: I read the code. check_merged asks Host::merged_commit(link) and then compares the commit's fingerprint with the verified one. A mismatch returns MergeOutcome::MergedButNotVerified. No commit message is read, and the test asserts the host was asked for number 42.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. Tests pass for the guard refusing a non-fast-forward and a wrong branch, for a lookup by PR number on a merged commit with a trailing Co-authored-by paragraph and no Athena trailer, and for the mismatch result on a disjoint-file case.
criteria.evidence: All 5 pr tests passed in my run, including the_guard_refuses_a_non_fast_forward_push (with real git), the_guard_refuses_a_branch_that_is_not_the_jobs_own, the_merge_is_found_by_number_even_with_a_trailing_co_authored_by_paragraph and disjoint_file_merges_are_merged_but_not_verified. Athena's full `cargo test --locked` run also passed (332 tests).

findings.summary: The link file lives in the job's state directory, which clean_job deletes, so the stored PR number can be lost before the merge is seen.
findings.evidence: state.rs clean_job removes job_dir(job), and link_path is under job_dir. D86's Tradeoff already records this and leaves the fix to the command slice.

findings.summary: The push guard turns any git error into a NotFastForward refusal, so the reason it shows may be wrong (for example, git missing).
findings.evidence: `git.is_ancestor(remote, request.local_head).unwrap_or(false)`. The behaviour is safe and documented, but the error message can mislead.

findings.summary: Of the expected deliverables, store.rs, paths.rs and roadmap.md were not changed.
findings.evidence: The diffstat touches 6 files. A roadmap edit is out of scope anyway, and the module works without store.rs or paths.rs changes.

summary: The change passes. It amends the design to answer review 3's N1-N4, and N5's wording as well, and it adds `crates/athena-core/src/pr.rs`, a library with no callers yet. The module has three parts: a store for the pull request link (number, host, repository, pushed head, job id), kept in the job's state directory and not in the repository's records; a push guard that allows only the job's own branch, only as a fast-forward, with no force option; and a merged-content check that finds the merge by the stored pull request number and returns "merged but not verified" when the fingerprints differ. The 5 tests for this module passed when I ran them. They cover a push to the wrong branch, a non-fast-forward push (against real git), a lookup by number on a merged commit ending in a host Co-authored-by paragraph, and the disjoint-file mismatch. Clippy and the format check are clean. The design text answers each N item precisely. There are no CLI or `gh` calls, no stealth implementation, and no roadmap edit, as scoped. Two minor findings: the link file sits in the job's directory, which `clean_job` deletes (the decision record already notes this for the next slice), and the guard reports any git error as a non-fast-forward refusal, which is safe but can name the wrong reason.
